_provenance.bg_is_the_DEFAULT_HALF_AND_THAT_IS_A_LIM: What the `bg` pair proves: the contract gives ONE engine fact three legal document spellings — `bg` absent (eight rows), `bg.layoutRef` null (`sec3`), and `bg.layoutRef` "@act" (`sec0`) — and all three must flatten to the SAME row, `{layoutRef: null, span: null}`, i.e. Region.rg_bg_layout = 0 and rg_bg_span = 0. Both flatteners have to collapse the sentinel; a flattener that copied "@act" through would put a STRING where the engine dereferences a POINTER. That collapse is the one thing about these two fields a seam test can check today, and it is now checked from both sides. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, said plainly so nobody reads it as more: NO ROW HERE CARRIES A NON-DEFAULT BACKGROUND, so nothing here would fail against a flattener that computed rg_bg_layout/rg_bg_span for a NAMED layout wrongly. That half is blocked, not skipped, and it is blocked on three measured things at aeon 9332c1af: (1) tools/effects_gen.py refuses a named `bg.layoutRef` outright, because nothing lowers this document into a region table yet (act 1's rows are hand-written); (2) the layout library games/sonic4/data/editor/ojz_bglib.json carries `id` and `name` and NO HEIGHT, so the derived-span check — which AURORA_REGIONS_SCHEMA.md section 5 calls the golden's whole reason for existing — has nothing to derive from; and (3) every id in that library is hyphenated and timestamped (`ingame-forest-v15-1786630615596`), which the contract's `bg.layoutRef` pattern `^(@act|[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31})$` cannot spell, so no REAL layout can be named in a schema-legal document at all. Booked in docs/DEFERRED_WORK.md under REGIONS-BG-GOLDEN-GAP; tools/test_regions_doc.py carries a tripwire that FAILS the day the refusal in (1) is lifted without this file growing the non-default row it then owes.
_provenance.row_9_id_is_RULED_not_transcribed: Row 9's id is `ojz_preset_night` by HUB RULING, empyrean a718ea7c docs/AURORA_REGIONS_SCHEMA.md, section "A KEY-LESS ROW'S ID IS ITS PRESET SYMBOL, LOWERCASED - AND AEON'S `night` MOVES" (2026-09-16T10:5xZ). Rows 0-8 are KEYED to sections and keep sec0..sec8; row 9 is KEY-LESS - aeon's descriptor rows carry no ids at all, so `night` was an English word this lane typed into a fixture and nothing derived it. The rule is: the preset symbol lowercased, [^a-z0-9_] folded to _, leading _ stripped, truncated to the schema pattern's 32. OJZ_Preset_Night -> ojz_preset_night. THE MINTING IS AURORA'S, NOT AEON'S: the id is written once by the migration and never re-derived, so a later preset rename leaves this id bound to some other preset - ugly, not broken, and stable, which is what `id` is for. Aeon does not implement the rule (a second implementation of a rule another tool owns is a drift source); tools/test_regions_doc.py derives the expectation from this file's own `preset` field instead. The readable label lives in the document's `name` field ("Night"), which is a CONDITION of the ruling and not a leftover.
_provenance.night_is_the_point: Row 9 straddles the section line at x = 4096 and neither of its edges (3400, 4800) lands on a multiple of the 2048 section size. It is in this fixture because a document whose regions all sit on the section grid cannot tell a correct flattener from one that quietly snaps to sections, and cannot exercise the two rows (`sec1`, `sec2`) whose spans are the night region's complement rather than a section's width.
